patch.value: GH-1597: expose host-bound item transaction status and safe abandonment or supersession

GitHub https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1597 requests public recovery for interrupted item-mutation journals when a peer edit changes the retry plan. Existing bulk commit and guarded compensation are shipped; extend their public host-bound lifecycle rather than duplicating private journal storage or reviving completed implementation.

Expose typed host-bound journal state and applied/compensated step receipts with plan identity; Provide safe abandonment and supersession using proven apply markers and existing guarded compensation; never overwrite later peer edits or silently compensate committed work; Name executable public recovery in transaction-plan-mismatch guidance and verify non-Git crash/retry/peer-edit controls plus SDK contract documentation
Extensions can inspect and recover interrupted batches through a supported root-bound API without reading private paths or recreating journal and compensation rules.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Native late-peer recovery oracle initially exposed a delete-store gap: the existing scoped item precondition was checked by update/close but not by locked deletion. Isolated candidate adds the same assertion before deletion policy/hooks and centralizes create compensation ownership checks. Close and delete both preserve a peer edit injected immediately before item-lock acquisition. Isolated focused proof passes51 tests; original checkout remains frozen for the in-flight full coverage run. Retirement intent is additionally retained before compensation to fence forward replay across recovery crashes.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Retiring an interrupted batch requires a durable intent before compensation, not only a terminal status afterward. Every destructive compensation must recheck ownership under the target item lock; a pre-lock history comparison alone does not protect a late peer edit.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Review remediation: CodeRabbit correctly identified that a durable supersession retry could be permanently blocked if another commit used the chosen replacement id after a crash. The extended final-journal-write interruption regression reproduced the refusal before the fix. Replacement freshness is now checked only when starting retirement; retries retain their original intent and finish without touching the replacement. Added an assertion that plan-mismatch guidance names client.itemTransactions.abandon. Documented journal value retention outside history-redact. Release/telemetry PM observations remain in this grouped delivery because the requested scope explicitly includes these audits; they are not new claims of infrastructure remediation.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Additional crash regression: a padded transaction id was normalized by the coordinator but not by item-history markers. The extended existing prepared/applied/recorded table proved that applied and recorded attempts could retire while leaving the forward value unchanged. Normalize identity once before building any item step, unique-key index or journal. Local transport admission remains failed; a separately built unchanged base commit also fails all six transport budgets on this host, while the isolated candidate SDK import-cost gate passes. Thresholds are unchanged; exact-head hosted transport admission is required.

patch.value: Packages can inspect and safely retire interrupted item batches through their configured client without rebuilding private journal rules.

Implemented bound status, abandon and supersede APIs with retained original plans, versioned durable retirement intent, idempotent audit and guarded compensation that preserves peer edits.
